control_gap: The cache key cannot represent both same-named files.

evidence.observation: The scan result is keyed by basename.

impact: One document can silently replace another in scan/index state, producing incomplete retrieval and ambiguous deletion.
remediation_seed: Key documents by canonical relative path or immutable document ID and migrate existing cache metadata with collision detection.
reproducibility: Create two synthetic same-named files under separate sandbox subdirectories and compare scan/document results.
root_cause: KnowledgeCache._scan keys discovered documents by path.name rather than a unique relative path or content identity.
title: Knowledge documents collide by basename
trigger_conditions: Two supported files in different subdirectories have the same basename

control_gap: No-result semantics are replaced by arbitrary fallback and no user-facing uncertainty guarantee exists.

evidence.observation: No-match behavior selects the leading cached sections.
Ranking is lexical and can return no relevant match.

existing_controls: Lexical matches are ranked when present
impact: The model can receive irrelevant or wrong-category material and present an unsupported answer with apparent knowledge grounding.
remediation_seed: Return an explicit no-result state, preserve knowledge type, and require uncertainty/citation behavior when support is absent.
reproducibility: Build a synthetic cache with unrelated sections and query with disjoint tokens; inspect constructed context.
root_cause: When lexical search finds no relevant section, context construction falls back to the first bounded set of cached sections instead of returning no support.
title: Lexical retrieval miss injects arbitrary leading sections
trigger_conditions: A query has no lexical overlap with indexed knowledge

control_gap: Atomic replacement does not serialize the shared staging path or cross-process state.

evidence.observation: Persistence uses a fixed temporary path before replace.

existing_controls: Final replacement is atomic on supported filesystems
Cache load can recover from some corruption
impact: Concurrent writers can overwrite staging bytes, fail replacement, or persist a cache that does not correspond to either worker's index state.
remediation_seed: Use unique temporary files plus an inter-process lock/version check, or move shared cache state to a concurrency-safe store.
reproducibility: In an isolated copy only, coordinate two processes writing distinct synthetic cache states and compare outcomes.
root_cause: KnowledgeCache.save writes through one predictable .tmp path without inter-process locking or unique staging names.
title: Knowledge cache persistence uses a shared fixed temporary filename
trigger_conditions: Two workers save or refresh the same cache concurrently

control_gap: There is no structural separation, content policy scan, provenance-based trust tier, or deterministic exclusion of instruction-like context.

evidence.observation: Cross-session text is selected for prompt use.
Memory, summaries, history, and knowledge are assembled into the model prompt.

impact: Poisoned context can steer output, expose adjacent context, or alter safety behavior on later turns.
remediation_seed: Apply ingestion and retrieval safety policies, structured data channels, provenance/trust tiers, and least-context assembly.
reproducibility: Store synthetic instruction-like memory/knowledge in a sandbox and inspect the generated prompt and fake-model behavior.
root_cause: Long-term memories, cross-session snippets, summaries, and knowledge are concatenated into model context; containment relies primarily on textual prompt instructions.
title: Memory and retrieved text are only prompt-labeled as untrusted
trigger_conditions: Stored or retrieved content contains instructions or adversarial text
The model follows data-plane instructions over policy

control_gap: Internal provenance does not become a stable claim-to-source mapping or freshness indicator.

evidence.observation: Generated reply does not enforce citations.

existing_controls: Prompt can receive rendered source information
impact: Users and reviewers may be unable to distinguish grounded guidance from model synthesis or trace a claim to a maintained source.
non_reproducibility_reason: The future user-harm likelihood depends on generated claims; the missing citation contract is repository-proven.
remediation_seed: Propagate document IDs/version timestamps through retrieval and require claim-level citations or explicit ungrounded uncertainty.
reproducibility: Static trace; no live generated claims were tested.
root_cause: Cached sections retain source metadata internally, but normal response generation has no repository-proven citation or support-verification contract exposed to users.
title: Knowledge provenance is not carried to user-visible responses
trigger_conditions: Knowledge-backed answer is wrong, stale, or contested
Users need to verify mental-health or operational guidance
